text:
A couple longed for a baby for many years. When their wish finally came true, a greedy witch demanded the baby as payment for herbs the couple had stolen from her garden.

The tiny girl was named Rapunzel, and the witch took her away at birth.

The witch locked Rapunzel in a tall stone tower in the middle of a forest. There were no stairs and no door — only one high window. Rapunzel grew up alone, singing songs and watching the world far below.

She had one extraordinary gift: golden hair that grew incredibly long.

Every day the witch called up: "Rapunzel, Rapunzel — let down your golden hair!" And Rapunzel would unroll her braid out the window like a rope for the witch to climb.

Rapunzel had never seen anyone else in her whole life.

One day, a young prince rode through the forest and heard the most beautiful singing drifting from the tower. He circled the tower for days, wondering how to get in. Then one morning he hid and watched as the witch called up to the tower...

The next day, the Prince called out in the witch's voice: "Rapunzel, Rapunzel — let down your hair!" The golden braid tumbled down, and up he climbed.

Rapunzel had never seen a young man before. They were shy at first, but soon became dear friends.

The witch discovered their friendship and flew into a rage! She cut off Rapunzel's braid and banished her to a distant desert. Then she waited for the Prince.

When he climbed up, the witch let the braid drop. He fell from the tower into thorns below, and lost his sight.

Blind and heartbroken, the Prince wandered for years. One day he heard a familiar voice singing. It was Rapunzel!

She ran to him and wept tears of joy that fell onto his eyes. When she wiped them away, his sight was RESTORED. Love had healed him completely.

Rapunzel and the Prince returned to his kingdom together. She finally saw the world she had only dreamed of from her tower window — and found it even more wonderful than she had imagined.

🌟 THE END 🌟

💡 Moral: Hope and love can set you free!
